subject: physics

concepts.title: Electrostatic Potential and Potential Difference
concepts.definition: The electric potential at a point represents the external work needed per unit positive charge to bring it from infinity to that point without acceleration.
concepts.formula: V = W / q, Delta_V = V_P - V_R = W_RP / q
concepts.key_idea: Electric potential difference is the path-independent work done per unit test charge between two points in an electric field.
question_patterns: calculate the electrostatic potential at a point given the work done and test charge
find the work required to move a charge between two points of known potential difference
what is the potential difference between two terminals given work and charge
how much work is done in bringing a charge from infinity to a point
solve a numerical on electrostatic potential and potential difference

solution_steps.action: calculate work done using charge and potential difference
solution_steps.explain: work done equals the product of the magnitude of charge and the potential difference between the endpoints

solution_steps.action: calculate electric potential at a point from work and charge
solution_steps.explain: potential equals work done per unit charge to bring the test charge from infinity

solution_steps.action: find potential difference between two points
solution_steps.explain: potential difference is the work done per unit charge moving between the two points

concepts.title: Potential due to a Point Charge
concepts.definition: The electric potential produced by an isolated point charge at a radial distance varies in direct proportion with the source charge and in inverse proportion with the distance.
concepts.key_idea: The potential of a point charge falls off as 1/r with distance and keeps the algebraic sign of the charge.
question_patterns: calculate the potential at a point due to a point charge located at a distance
find the electric potential at a given distance from a point charge
what is the potential produced by a charge at a specified separation
how much is the electric potential at distance r from charge Q
find the required value in a potential due to a point charge problem

solution_steps.action: compute electric potential from point charge
solution_steps.explain: use Coulomb constant k = 9e9 N m^2 / C^2 multiplied by charge and divided by distance

solution_steps.action: determine the sign of the potential from the charge sign
solution_steps.explain: potential is positive for positive charges and negative for negative charges since it carries the algebraic sign of the source charge

solution_steps.action: calculate work done to bring a test charge from infinity to the point
solution_steps.explain: work done equals the test charge multiplied by the potential at that point

concepts.title: Potential due to an Electric Dipole
concepts.definition: The electrostatic potential created by an electric dipole at large distances varies with the dipole moment, the angle with the dipole axis, and falls off inversely with the distance's square.
concepts.key_idea: Dipole potential falls as 1/r^2 and vanishes everywhere along the equatorial plane where theta is 90 degrees.
question_patterns: calculate the electric potential due to a dipole at a point on its axis
find the dipole potential at a given angle and distance
what is the electric potential on the equatorial plane of a dipole
determine the potential at distance r from a short electric dipole
what is the result in this potential due to an electric dipole problem

solution_steps.action: calculate the dipole potential
solution_steps.explain: multiply Coulomb constant by dipole moment and cosine of angle, divided by distance squared

solution_steps.action: evaluate the potential on the equatorial plane
solution_steps.explain: on the equatorial plane theta is 90 degrees so cos(theta) is zero and the dipole potential vanishes

solution_steps.action: find the distance dependence of the dipole potential
solution_steps.explain: unlike a point charge, the dipole potential falls off as 1/r^2 with distance due to the cancellation of monopole terms

concepts.title: Potential due to a System of Charges and Superposition
concepts.definition: The total electrostatic potential at a point due to a collection of point charges is the algebraic sum of the potentials produced by each charge individually.
concepts.key_idea: Electric potential is a scalar quantity, so multiple contributions add algebraically with their proper signs.
question_patterns: calculate the net potential at the center of a polygon with charges at the vertices
find the point along the line joining two charges where the net potential is zero
what is the total potential at a point due to multiple discrete charges
determine the algebraic sum of electric potentials at a given observation point
work out the value using potential due to a system of charges and superposition

solution_steps.action: calculate potential contribution from each charge
solution_steps.explain: compute individual potentials using k * q / r and sum them up

solution_steps.action: include the algebraic sign of each charge in the sum
solution_steps.explain: potential is a scalar so each contribution keeps the sign of its source charge and adds algebraically

solution_steps.action: find the point where net potential is zero
solution_steps.explain: set the algebraic sum of individual potentials to zero and solve for the unknown position

concepts.title: Equipotential Surfaces and Electric Field Relation
concepts.definition: An equipotential surface is a geometric locus of all points having identical electric potential, which is always oriented perpendicular to the local electric field lines.
concepts.key_idea: The electric field points in the direction where potential decreases most rapidly, and no work is indeed required to move charges across an equipotential surface.
question_patterns: identify the equipotential surfaces for a uniform field or point charge
calculate electric field magnitude from potential gradient
what is the relation between electric field and potential difference between two surfaces
find the magnitude of electric field given change in potential over distance
compute the answer step by step for equipotential surfaces and electric field relation

solution_steps.action: calculate electric field magnitude from potential difference and separation
solution_steps.explain: electric field magnitude equals potential difference divided by normal separation

solution_steps.action: determine the direction of the electric field relative to potential
solution_steps.explain: the electric field points in the direction where potential decreases most rapidly, hence the negative sign in E = -dV/dl

solution_steps.action: verify that no work is needed to move a charge along an equipotential surface
solution_steps.explain: on an equipotential surface the potential difference is zero so the work done is zero and the field is perpendicular to the surface

concepts.title: Potential Energy of a System of Charges
concepts.definition: The work an external agency must do to assemble a set of charges from infinitely far apart, placing each at its position; that stored work is the configuration's electrostatic potential energy.
concepts.key_idea: Pairwise interaction energies add up to give the total potential energy of a multi-charge system.
question_patterns: calculate the electrostatic potential energy of a pair of charges
find the work required to assemble or separate a system of charges
determine the total interaction energy of charges placed at the corners of a geometric shape
how much work is needed to separate two point charges to infinity
what is the result in this potential energy of a system of charges problem

solution_steps.action: compute electrostatic potential energy of two charges
solution_steps.explain: multiply Coulomb constant with the product of charges divided by their separation

solution_steps.action: find work required to separate charges to infinity
solution_steps.explain: work done to separate charges completely is the negative of the bound potential energy

solution_steps.action: sum pairwise interaction energies for a multi-charge system
solution_steps.explain: for more than two charges, add the potential energy of every unique pair to get the total configuration energy

concepts.title: Potential Energy of a Dipole in an External Field
concepts.definition: The potential energy kept in an electric dipole oriented inside a uniform external electric field depends on the scalar product of its dipole moment and the field vector.
concepts.formula: U = - p * E * cos(theta), W = p * E * (cos(theta_0) - cos(theta_1))
concepts.key_idea: The dipole has minimum energy in stable alignment parallel to the both field and maximum energy when antiparallel.
question_patterns: calculate the potential energy of an electric dipole in an external electric field
find the work done to rotate a dipole from one angle to another in a uniform field
estimate the heat released when polarized dipoles reorient in an altered field direction
what is the change in potential energy when a dipole rotates by an angle
find the required value in a potential energy of a dipole in an external field problem

solution_steps.action: calculate initial potential energy
solution_steps.explain: potential energy is negative dipole moment times electric field times cos of initial angle

solution_steps.action: calculate final potential energy
solution_steps.explain: potential energy at final angle

solution_steps.action: find difference or work done
solution_steps.explain: change in energy equals final minus initial energy

concepts.title: Electrostatics of Conductors and Electrostatic Shielding
concepts.definition: In static equilibrium, conductors exhibit zero internal electric field, constant internal potential matching the surface, surface-only excess charge, and zero field inside charge-free cavities.
concepts.formula: E_inside = 0, E_surface = sigma / epsilon_0, V_inside = V_surface = const
concepts.key_idea: A metallic enclosure completely shields any internal cavity from outside electrostatic fields regardless of external charge or voltage.
question_patterns: explain why the electric field inside a conductor in static equilibrium is zero
show that all excess charge on a conductor resides entirely on its outer surface
describe the principle and applications of electrostatic shielding
verify that electrostatic potential is constant throughout the volume of a conductor
why is electrostatics of conductors and electrostatic shielding important

solution_steps.action: analyze equilibrium condition of free mobile charges
solution_steps.explain: if internal electric field were non-zero, free electrons would experience force and accelerate; in static state no current flows, implying net internal field must be zero everywhere

solution_steps.action: apply Gauss law to an internal Gaussian surface
solution_steps.explain: since electric flux is zero through any closed surface inside the conductor material, the net enclosed charge is zero, proving excess charges reside on the outer surface

solution_steps.action: establish constancy of potential
solution_steps.explain: zero internal electric field implies line integral of field between any two points vanishes, keeping electric potential uniform across the body and surface

concepts.title: Parallel Plate Capacitor
concepts.definition: A parallel plate capacitor is indeed made up of two planar conducting sheets separated by a dielectric medium, storing charge and electrostatic field energy between them.
concepts.formula: C = epsilon_0 * A / d, Q = C * V
concepts.key_idea: Capacitance depends only on the geometry of the conducting plates and the permittivity of the medium between them.
question_patterns: calculate the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor in vacuum
find the charge on capacitor plates connected to a given voltage source
what plate area is needed to achieve a desired capacitance at a fixed separation
determine the potential difference across a parallel plate capacitor
calculate parallel plate capacitor for the given values

solution_steps.action: calculate capacitance of parallel plate capacitor
solution_steps.explain: multiply permittivity of free space by plate area and divide by plate separation

solution_steps.action: calculate charge on the capacitor
solution_steps.explain: multiply capacitance by voltage across the plates

solution_steps.action: calculate the plate area needed for a desired capacitance
solution_steps.explain: rearrange C = epsilon_0 * A / d to solve for area given the target capacitance and fixed separation

concepts.title: Dielectric Insertion in Capacitors
concepts.definition: Introducing an insulating dielectric material of dielectric constant K between capacitor plates polarizes the dielectric, reducing the internal electric field and multiplying capacitance by factor K.
concepts.formula: C = K * C_0, C_0 = epsilon_0 * A / d
concepts.key_idea: Dielectrics reduce the potential difference for an isolated charged capacitor or increase the stored charge at a constant supply voltage.
question_patterns: calculate the new capacitance when a dielectric slab is inserted
find the factor by which capacitance changes when separation is halved and dielectric is introduced
what is the effect of dielectric insertion on charge and potential difference
determine the dielectric constant from vacuum and filled capacitance values
find the required value in a dielectric insertion in capacitors problem

solution_steps.action: compute modified capacitance with dielectric and new geometry
solution_steps.explain: scale base capacitance by dielectric constant and inverse of plate separation factor

solution_steps.action: find the dielectric constant from vacuum and filled capacitance values
solution_steps.explain: the dielectric constant equals the ratio of the filled capacitance to the vacuum capacitance

solution_steps.action: determine the effect of dielectric on an isolated charged capacitor
solution_steps.explain: for an isolated capacitor the charge stays fixed so inserting a dielectric reduces the potential difference by the factor K

concepts.title: Combinations of Capacitors
concepts.definition: Multiple capacitors connected end-to-end in series share identical charge with reciprocal addition of capacitances, while in parallel they share identical voltage with direct addition of capacitances.
concepts.key_idea: Series combinations decrease the overall equivalent capacitance while parallel arrangements increase the equivalent capacitance.
question_patterns: calculate the equivalent capacitance of capacitors connected in series
find the total capacitance of a parallel combination of capacitors
determine the voltage across each capacitor in a series circuit
calculate the charge on individual capacitors in a parallel network
what is the result in this combinations of capacitors problem

solution_steps.action: calculate equivalent capacitance for series combination
solution_steps.explain: for n identical capacitors in series, divide single capacitance by number of capacitors

solution_steps.action: calculate equivalent capacitance for parallel combination
solution_steps.explain: sum individual capacitances

solution_steps.action: calculate the charge on each capacitor in the combination
solution_steps.explain: in series each capacitor holds the same charge equal to the equivalent capacitance times the supply voltage, while in parallel each holds charge equal to its own capacitance times the common voltage

concepts.title: Electrostatic Energy Stored in a Capacitor and Energy Density
concepts.definition: The energy stored in a charged capacitor is the total work done during the charging process, residing in the localized electrostatic field with an energy density proportional to the square of the field strength.
concepts.key_idea: Energy is stored within the electrostatic field itself, and charge sharing between capacitors generally results in dissipative energy loss.
question_patterns: calculate the electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor
find the energy lost when a charged capacitor is connected to an uncharged capacitor
calculate the energy density of an electric field
determine the total stored energy given charge and voltage
solve a numerical on electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor and energy density

solution_steps.action: calculate stored electrostatic energy
solution_steps.explain: stored energy equals one half times capacitance times voltage squared

solution_steps.action: calculate energy loss on connecting to identical uncharged capacitor
solution_steps.explain: common potential becomes half and final total energy becomes half of initial stored energy

solution_steps.action: calculate the energy density of the electric field
solution_steps.explain: energy density equals one half times the permittivity of free space times the electric field squared

Two charges 2 micro-C and -2 micro-C are placed at points A and B 6 cm apart. (a) Identify an equipotential surface of the system. (b) What is the direction of the electric field at every point on this surface?

A spherical conductor of radius 12 cm has a charge of 1.6 * 10^-7 C distributed uniformly on its surface. What is the electric field (a) inside the sphere (b) just outside the sphere (c) at a point 18 cm from the centre of the sphere?

A parallel plate capacitor with air between the plates has a capacitance of 8 pF. What will be the capacitance if the distance between the plates is reduced by half, and the space between them is filled with a substance of dielectric constant 6?

Three capacitors each of capacitance 9 pF are connected in series. (a) What is the total capacitance of the combination? (b) What is the potential difference across each capacitor if the combination is connected to a 120 V supply?

Three capacitors of capacitances 2 pF, 3 pF and 4 pF are connected in parallel. (a) What is the total capacitance of the combination? (b) Determine the charge on each capacitor if the combination is connected to a 100 V supply.

In a parallel plate capacitor with air between the plates, each plate has an area of 6 * 10^-3 m^2 and the distance between the plates is 3 mm. Calculate the capacitance of the capacitor. If this capacitor is connected to a 100 V supply, what is the charge on each plate of the capacitor?

Explain what would happen if in the capacitor given in Exercise 2.8, a 3 mm thick mica sheet (of dielectric constant = 6) were inserted between the plates, (a) while the voltage supply remained connected, (b) after the supply was disconnected.
